ap_chemistry-m01.stem: A student heats a hydrated salt in a crucible to find the formula of the hydrate. Which step best ensures that all of the water has been removed before the final mass is recorded?

options.text: Reheat the crucible and weigh it again, repeating until two successive masses agree.
options.why: Masses that no longer change show that no more water is leaving the sample.

options.text: Add a few drops of water and weigh the sample while it is still wet.
options.why: Extra water adds mass and defeats the purpose of drying.

options.text: Heat the sample for exactly one minute and weigh it once.
options.why: A fixed time does not show that the sample is dry.

options.text: Weigh the crucible while it is still very hot to save time.
options.why: A hot crucible produces air currents that make the mass reading inaccurate.

ap_chemistry-m02.stem: Two liquids, X and Y, are at the same temperature. Liquid X has a much higher surface tension than liquid Y. Which statement about the intermolecular forces is most reasonable?

options.text: The forces between molecules of X are stronger than those between molecules of Y.
options.why: Surface tension is higher when molecules at the surface are pulled inward more strongly by their neighbors.

options.text: The molecules of X have a higher average kinetic energy than those of Y.
options.why: The liquids are at the same temperature, so their average kinetic energies are equal.

options.text: The forces between molecules of X are weaker than between molecules of Y.
options.why: Weaker forces give a lower, not a higher, surface tension.

options.text: The covalent bonds inside the molecules of X are broken at the surface.
options.why: Surface tension does not involve breaking bonds within molecules.

facts: Two liquids, X and Y, are at the same temperature. Liquid X

ap_chemistry-m03.stem: Water vapor at 110 °C is cooled at a constant rate to 80 °C. The temperature stays at 100 °C for a time. What is happening to the water molecules during that time?

options.text: The molecules are condensing: attractions form, energy is released, and the average kinetic energy is unchanged.
options.why: During a phase change at constant temperature, the potential energy changes while the average kinetic energy is constant.

options.text: The molecules are breaking into hydrogen and oxygen atoms.
options.why: Condensation is a physical change and does not break bonds within molecules.

options.text: The molecules are slowing down on average because the sample is losing energy.
options.why: The temperature is constant, so the average kinetic energy is constant.

options.text: The molecules stop moving entirely until the sample is cooler.
options.why: Molecules in a liquid keep moving at 100 °C.

facts: Water vapor at 110 °C is cooled at a constant rate to 80 °C.

Uses the pH value instead of [H⁺] in the expression.
